title: Transport a glueing morphism across localized isomorphisms
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ any ring map, $t\in\mathbf N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] have at every $M$ the prime module $S\otimes_R M$ [def-weil-module-base-change], chart modules $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and actual canonical comparison and interchange linear maps, through bundled module equalities and heterogeneous linear-map equalities. All modules lie in universe $\max(u,v,w)$, with $R,S$ in universes $u,v$. Let $H,E$ be $R$-modules, $X$ a glueing datum, $\psi:\mathrm{Can}(H)\to X$ a glueing morphism with bijective chart maps, $j:H\to E$ an $R$-linear map whose localizations $j_{f_i}$ are bijective, and $\theta:S\otimes_R E\overset\sim\longrightarrow X.M'$ an $S$-linear equivalence. Assume $\theta\circ(S\otimes_R j)=\psi'$ via the canonical prime-module identification. Then there is a glueing morphism $\Phi:\mathrm{Can}(E)\to X$ whose prime map and every chart map are bijective. No flatness, ideal-quotient comparison, or assumption about Can on morphisms is required.

proof.text: Use canonical_functor_maps on Can.obj and the supplied canonical object identifications to obtain a morphism F : Can(H) → Can(E) whose prime map is extendMap φ j and whose chart maps are localMap (f i) j, through heterogeneous equality. Only this prescribed morphism is used; no property of Can.map is assumed. Identify each restricted canonical chart with localize (f i) using module extensionality and algebraMap_smul. Transport bijectivity of localMap j to F.chart. Transport theta along the prime-module equality to an equivalence p and use the heterogeneous equations to prove p composed with F.prime = psi.prime.

For arbitrary glueing objects A, B, X and morphisms F : A → B and psi : A → X as above, define each new chart as psi.chart composed with the inverse of the bijective F.chart and the prime map as p. Tensor base change preserves surjections (Mathlib LinearMap.baseChange_surjective), so the prime compatibility of F and the structural alpha equivalences imply that localizing F.prime is surjective. Precompose the proposed prime compatibility with this surjection: preservation of composition under localization and scalar extension, the equation p composed with F.prime = psi.prime, the chart inverse identity, and the compatibilities of F and psi prove the equation. Only surjectivity, rather than bijectivity, is needed for cancellation.

Localization preserves surjections (Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.map_surjective). Precompose each proposed overlap compatibility with the localization of F.chart i. The chart inverse identities, preservation of composition, and overlap compatibilities of F and psi prove the equation; cancel the surjection. Bundle these two equations into the desired Hom. The prime map is the transported theta equivalence and the chart maps are composites of bijections. For t = 0 the compatibility and chart assertions are vacuous and the prime equivalence suffices.

theorem exists_extension_transport {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (H E : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (ψ : Can.obj H ⟶ X) (j : H →ₗ[R] E)
    (θ : extend φ E ≃ₗ[S] X.M')
    (hj : ∀ i, Function.Bijective (localMap (f i) j))
    (hψ : ∀ i, Function.Bijective (ψ.chart i))
    (hθ : HEq (θ.toLinearMap.comp (extendMap φ j)) ψ.prime) :
    ∃ Φ : Can.obj E ⟶ X,
      Function.Bijective Φ.prime ∧ ∀ i, Function.Bijective (Φ.chart i)
